title: Is Winter Really Killing Your Vitamin D?
description:
Is winter vitamin D loss real? It's dark around 5 in Toronto now, but Canadian studies found the summer-to-winter dip was small. Supplements and ancestry mattered way more. Cyto breaks it down from the 6ix.

In a Vancouver study, vitamin D was only about 12 nmol/L higher in summer than in winter. A Health Canada study found supplement use and ancestry made bigger differences than season, and low vitamin D was more common in South Asian Canadians than in European-ancestry Canadians across the seasons tested. The dark can still hit your mood: seasonal depression is real for some people, and a 2025 review of 17 trials found bright white light came out on top among light colours.

Sources (PubMed):
Li et al., Can J Public Health 2011 — https://doi.org/10.1007/BF03404056
Nagasaka et al., PLoS One 2018 — https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0207429
Wan et al., Medicine 2025 — https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000043107

Not medical advice. Low mood lasting 2+ weeks or worried about low vitamin D? Talk to a doctor or pharmacist.
